source.title: Synaptic mechanisms and network dynamics underlying spatial working memory in a cortical network model

confidence_rationale: The canonical recurrent-attractor ('bump attractor') mechanistic model of how persistent delay activity is sustained: strong recurrent excitation (NMDA-dominated) balanced by inhibition holds a self-sustaining activity bump with no external input. Strongly supports fork A as a MECHANISM for maintaining the engaged item. Marked mixed for ARC-063 because the same model exposes fork A's ceiling for the CRF's problem: an attractor network holds ONE bump (a few items at most), is metabolically expensive (tonic high-rate firing), and is prone to drift/interference -- it does not scale to silently holding a differentiated POOL of 10-16 sparsely-matching rules, which is exactly the CRF regime in V3-EXQ-666 ARM_2.
failure_signatures: A continuous-attractor (bump) network sustains a single localized activity packet; capacity is small and adding more simultaneously-active memoranda causes bumps to merge or compete. It cannot maintain a large pool of distinct currently-unselected rules by persistent firing.

Persistent-firing maintenance is metabolically costly (all maintained items fire tonically at elevated rates for the whole delay) and the bump drifts over time and is disrupted by distractors -- arguing against per-tick sustained firing as the maintenance substrate for an availability POOL that must persist across thousands of ticks.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Selective persistent activity underlying spatial working memory can be generated and sustained by a cortical network with structured recurrent excitation (slow NMDA-receptor-mediated) and feedback inhibition: the network settles into a self-sustaining localized activity bump that survives the removal of the external cue, reproducing Funahashi-type delay activity.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the mechanistic 'how' for fork A. If the CRF were to maintain a rule by sustained activity, this is the circuit motif it would implement: a recurrent term that keeps a matched rule's availability self-reinforcing after the context disappears. It is directly relevant to a possible CRF fix (a sustained-activity term on the selected rule).
mapping.mapping_caveat: The attractor mechanism is single-bump and capacity-limited by construction -- it is a good model for holding ONE engaged rule but a poor model for the CRF's actual need (a differentiated pool of many rules that each match sparsely and are mostly unselected). Tonic-firing maintenance also costs energy proportional to the number of maintained items and drifts/decays under interference; the CRF must hold its pool across ~2000-3900 ticks. So this paper supplies fork A's mechanism but simultaneously bounds its applicability away from the CRF's pool-maintenance problem.
mapping.source_context: Spiking cortical network simulation (integrate-and-fire neurons, NMDA/AMPA/GABA synapses) tuned to the macaque dlPFC oculomotor delayed-response setting.

confidence_components.notes: Landmark, widely-reproduced computational model -- high source_quality. mapping_fidelity moderate: it is the right mechanism for fork A but the wrong scale for the CRF pool. transfer_risk elevated because a continuous spatial attractor maps only loosely onto a discrete slot-based rule field; the transferable idea is 'recurrent self-sustaining maintenance of the engaged item', not the bump geometry.
